test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Electrician) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: When using a multimeter to measure current, which of the following options is correct?

options.text: The multimeter is connected in parallel with the load.
The multimeter is connected only between resistive components.
The multimeter is connected in series with the load.
The multimeter is connected directly to the power source.

solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Correct Option Analysis:**

The correct option is:

**Option 3:** The multimeter is connected in series with the load.

When measuring current using a multimeter, it is crucial to connect the multimeter in series with the load. This configuration ensures that the current flowing through the load also flows through the multimeter, allowing it to accurately measure the current. Current is defined as the flow of electric charge through a conductor, and it is measured in amperes (A). Since the current remains constant throughout a series circuit, connecting the multimeter in series ensures that it measures the exact current flowing through the load.

**Why Series Connection Is Correct:**

 
• In a series connection, all components share the same current. Therefore, placing the multimeter in series with the load enables it to measure the current accurately.
 
• The multimeter has an internal resistance designed to be as low as possible in current measurement mode. This minimizes the effect on the circuit and ensures accurate readings.
 
• If the multimeter were connected in parallel with the load, it would create a short circuit due to its low internal resistance, potentially damaging the multimeter or the circuit.

**Steps to Measure Current Using a Multimeter:**

 
• Turn off the power supply to the circuit to ensure safe handling and measurement.
 
• Set the multimeter to the appropriate current measurement mode (AC or DC, depending on the type of current in the circuit).
 
• Break the circuit at the point where you want to measure the current and connect the multimeter in series with the load.
 
• Restore the power supply and observe the current reading on the multimeter display.

**Applications of Measuring Current:**

 
• Diagnosing electrical faults in circuits.
 
• Verifying the current consumption of electronic devices.
 
• Ensuring circuit components operate within their rated current limits.
